questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications at recommended doses will not affect your driving.
Medications prescribed by a doctor are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications — prescription or over-the-counter — can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and affect your ability to drive safely. It is your job to know how your medication affects your driving.

questions.question: If you drive slower than traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from:

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. This sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Only cars next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only cars next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When yellow lines are both solid and dashed, only cars next to the dashed line can cross it to pass. Cars next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages your judgment. Good judgment helps you react to things you see and hear on the road. Even below the legal limit, any amount of alcohol can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: Speeding too fast:

options.text: Gets you to your destination faster.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor decisions while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and prevent brake damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An octagon (eight-sided) sign always means "Stop." Come to a complete stop, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is clear.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you before going.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black words means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-way, two-lane road where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.
As your speed increases, so should your following distance.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds above 80 mph, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Faster speeds also require longer stopping distance, so you must increase your following distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and expressway ramps where you cannot enter. It tells you not to go in that direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right at an intersection where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangular signs mean yield. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed. If you stop, do so at the marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to what is ahead. This sign warns you that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must and must not do. Where this sign is posted, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. People may step out of parked vehicles or between them without looking. Other drivers may pull out without seeing you.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not tailgate. Increase your following distance.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Not watching carefully for workers and moving equipment

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch for workers and machines.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Over your left or right shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Lower your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning and keep tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking reserved for people with disabilities

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for people with disabilities
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates, disabled veteran plates, or disabled parking permits.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, pay attention, and proceed with caution. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles move.

questions.question: As daylight fades, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades so others can see you. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water
Shift into neutral while driving through the water

questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic may merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is entering from another road. Give drivers space to merge safely.
Traffic is entering from another road. Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Give drivers space to merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is merging into your lane. Check your side and rear, move to another lane if possible, and give merging drivers a clear path.
